title: Dam Break Inundation Modelling Using Hydrodynamic Modelling of any River
dataset_link: Open source Remote Sensing data (Sentinel, Landsat or any open source satellite image) and ASTER/ STRM or any other DEM.
description:
• Background In India, due to natural disaster various natural dam / lake formations were observed which can be a major reason of flash flood in the lower catchment, for example, natural lake formed over the Rishi Ganga river of Uttarakhand in Feb 2021, Wapriyang river in Nov 2021, Phuktal river near Sumdo, J&K in Mar 15, Kosi river in 2008 etc. Devastating flood happened in the Kashmir valley, Assam in 2014 and many other places over a period of time. Therefore, simulation modelling for flash flood and scenario generation is important from Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) point of view. Another important aspect is water release issues from the Dam of major rivers. In the crisis situation, if the dam brakes, how much water will flow into the river and what are the area it will inundated / impacted need to be estimated. In order to carry out this work simulation modelling needs to be done for the same. In other way if any dam break situation happened then what will be the impacted area. Development of a modelling framework is required which will carry out simulation modelling for the same.
• Description The above problem statement envisages that a software tool need to be developed which should automatically carry out the simulation modelling for Dam break analysis and identify the inundated area due to flash flood in the lower catchment. The modelling framework should be developed using hydrological data, DEM and satellite imagery of any river. The software/ tools should be capable of carrying out the simulation modelling of water flow in case of dam break or water release through ‘Smooth Particle Hydrodynamics’ and ‘Delf3D’ model and compare the scenario.
• Expected Solution/Deliverables The proposed study aims to illustrate the current problems regarding framework generation of Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief using simulation modelling related to flood management as follows:
i. Creation of generalized modelling framework to predict / simulate dam break/ river blockage analysis providing the necessary inputs on the basis of sudden water surge as well as loss and damage analysis using ‘Smooth Particle Hydrodynamics model and Delf3D model’.
ii. Building a customized tool/ framework so that it is possible to generate a flood inundation simulation scenario using different input datasets.
iii. Developing a Dashboard for providing modelling input and output visualization framework (GUI). The program should support the large volume of data. Output should be converted to .shp or .Kml file.
iv. Additionally, developing a framework for near real time flood analysis through Google Earth Engine with the help of open source data.
v. Simulation needs to be done by taking the any river and Dam data (open source) of India during the final demonstration of the software.
summary: Innovation (3/5): draws on satellite applied to a disaster management problem, placing it in the moderate band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (4/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Disaster Management. Tech Depth (3/5): centers on model. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 18/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: Dam Break Inundation Modelling Using Hydrodynamic Modelling of any River

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a hydrodynamic simulation tool that models what happens if a dam breaks, or a natural landslide-dammed lake bursts, on any given river, showing exactly how much water flows out, how fast, and which areas downstream get flooded.
overview.why_it_matters: India has repeatedly seen natural dam formations from landslides that then break and cause devastating flash floods. Genuine simulation capability gives disaster response teams real advance planning ability for these scenarios.
pain_points: Natural dam/lake formations from landslides create real flash-flood risk that's currently hard to model in advance.
Dam-break scenarios need genuine hydrodynamic simulation, not simple flood extrapolation, to accurately predict impact.
No general-purpose modelling framework applies across different rivers/dam scenarios.
overview.background: India has repeatedly experienced natural dam/lake formations and dam-break scenarios causing devastating flash floods, but simulation capability for predicting inundation extent and severity isn't systematically available.
overview.whats_being_asked: A hydrodynamic modelling software tool simulating dam-break/natural-dam-break scenarios for any river, predicting water flow volume, speed, and downstream inundation extent.
expected_solution: Hydrodynamic simulation engine (1D/2D flow modeling) applicable to arbitrary river/terrain inputs.
Dam-break scenario parameterization (breach size, timing, reservoir volume).
Downstream inundation extent and timing prediction.
Visualization of impacted areas for HADR planning.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Moderate as scored. Hydrodynamic dam-break modeling is an established hydraulic engineering discipline (well-documented methods like HEC-RAS exist), the value is in genuine applicability across arbitrary rivers with accessible tooling.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Moderate. Achievable using established hydrodynamic modeling principles and open-source tools/libraries as a foundation, real effort in making it genuinely usable for arbitrary river inputs.

competitive_landscape.note: Requires genuine hydraulic engineering/hydrology domain knowledge, a specialized field distinct from typical software hackathon skills.

innovation.note: Established hydraulic engineering discipline, the value is genuine, accessible applicability across arbitrary river scenarios.

invention.note: Achievable using established hydrodynamic modeling principles as a foundation, real effort in generalizability and usability.

technical_feasibility.tag: Comfortable for a Scoped Test Case
technical_feasibility.note: Full generalizability across 'any river' isn't achievable in 36 hours, scope to one well-documented test river/scenario with real terrain data.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly supports HADR planning for a genuine, recurring disaster type in India.

architecture.note: A hydrodynamic simulation engine with terrain/scenario input and visualization output, well-understood hydraulic engineering pattern.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick for a team with hydraulic engineering/hydrology background. Scope to one well-documented real river with accessible terrain/discharge data, and validate your model's basic physical behavior against known hydraulic principles, rather than claiming genuine universal applicability to 'any river' untested.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Well-documented hydraulic engineering principles and some open-source hydrodynamic modeling tools exist to build on, real technical grounding available.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Claiming genuine universal applicability to 'any river' without testing across multiple genuinely different terrain/river scenarios would be an overclaim, scope your validation honestly.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Choose one well-documented real river with accessible terrain (DEM) and discharge data for your primary test case, and validate your model's basic hydraulic behavior (conservation of mass, plausible flow velocities) against known physical principles.

idea_0_4: Research established dam-break hydrodynamic modeling principles (shallow water equations, break parameterization approaches).
Source real terrain (DEM) and river/reservoir data for one specific, well-documented test river.
Split: one person on the hydrodynamic simulation engine, one on terrain data processing and visualization.
prototype_4_22: Build your hydrodynamic simulation engine (1D or simplified 2D flow modeling) grounded in real hydraulic principles.
Process your real terrain data for your test river scenario.
Start dam-break scenario parameterization (breach characteristics, reservoir volume).
integration_22_30: Connect terrain, scenario parameters, and simulation into one coherent pipeline.
Validate basic physical plausibility of your simulation output (conservation of mass, reasonable flow velocities and timing).
Build inundation-extent visualization on your real terrain.
polish_30_36: Build a clear map visualization showing predicted inundation extent and timing for your test scenario.
Rehearse presenting your model's physical validation and grounding in real hydraulic principles.
Prepare to discuss what would be needed to genuinely generalize to other rivers.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Validate your simulation's basic physical behavior explicitly, showing conservation of mass holds and flow velocities/timing are physically plausible for your test river's known characteristics, that physics-grounded validation is what separates a credible hydrodynamic model from a visually plausible flood-extent guess.

strengths: Well-documented hydraulic engineering principles provide real technical grounding.
Genuine, high-stakes disaster-preparedness relevance for a recurring problem in India.
weaknesses: Genuine universal applicability to 'any river' isn't achievable or testable in 36 hours, requires honest single-case scoping.
Requires genuine hydraulic engineering domain knowledge most software teams won't have.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: This PS needs genuine hydraulic engineering domain knowledge, without it, physical accuracy is hard to achieve or validate.
team_fit.approach: Choose one well-documented test river/scenario and validate basic physics before claiming any broader applicability.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Standard numerical simulation scaffolding and terrain-data processing/visualization.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Correctly implementing hydrodynamic simulation physics (shallow water equations, breach modeling) and validating physical plausibility, that requires real hydraulic engineering expertise.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-generated hydrodynamic model without real hydraulic engineering validation could produce visually plausible but physically wrong flood predictions, a serious issue for a disaster-planning tool.

data_resource_availability.status: Public terrain (DEM) data and some river discharge/reservoir data are available for many Indian rivers for a well-chosen test case.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Choose a well-documented historical dam-break or natural-dam-formation event (several are named in the PS background) where some real data and reported outcomes exist for comparison.

judge_qna.question: How do you know your simulation's physics are actually correct, not just producing plausible-looking flood maps?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Show your validation against known hydraulic principles, conservation of mass, physically reasonable flow velocities and arrival timing for your test river's real characteristics.
judge_qna.follow_up: How does your model's prediction compare to any real, historical dam-break event data if available?

judge_qna.question: How would this actually generalize to 'any river' as the problem statement asks?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Be honest about your single-case validation scope, and describe what generalization would require, terrain data availability, calibration against known discharge data for each new river.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's the biggest terrain characteristic that would break your current model's assumptions?
